Assessment updated with Beige Book: In line with the March 2019 FOMC statement, the Beige Book for Jan–Feb reports modest overall activity across retail, autos, tourism, real estate, restaurants, manufacturing, and staffing. Consumer spending was damped by harsh winter weather and higher credit costs, and manufacturing faced softer global demand, tariffs, and trade-policy uncertainty; the government shutdown also weighed on early-quarter activity. Labor markets remain tight with widespread worker shortages (IT, manufacturing, trucking, restaurants, construction), wages rising for both low- and high-skill jobs, and broader nonwage compensation, consistent with low unemployment and continued expansion potential but with capacity constraints. The January SLOOS shows marginal tightening in C&I and construction/land development standards, wider spreads in places, and weaker demand across several business and household categories; banks anticipated further tightening and highlighted collateral and consumer credit performance risks. Offsets include generally unchanged standards for GSE-eligible mortgages, HELOCs, and autos, and some easing for large firms/loan covenants. Taken together with muted inflation, these observations reinforce a patient policy stance and temper the otherwise constructive outlook. Net: still mildly positive, but closer to neutral than before.
